definition_zh: 友谊；朋友关系；友情；（团体、国家间的）友好关系
definition_en: the relationship between friends, based on mutual trust and goodwill
core_image: 两个孩子在院墙两边埋下同一颗种子，藤蔓翻过墙头缠在一起，谁也没有去剪断
scene: 两个邻村的少年各走一半的路，在界石旁交换午饭，谁也不欠谁。 The two boys from rival villages met at the boundary stone each day and shared their lunches, and that friendship outlasted the quarrel between their families.
sceneCN: 这里 friendship 指「朋友之间彼此信任、互相往来的关系」（第 1 个义项：平等者之间长期自愿的友好关系）；句意为两个敌对村庄的少年每天在界石旁分吃午饭，这份友情比两家人的争吵更长久。可辨识物件：界石、饭盒、半旧书包、田埂。

senses.title: A bond two people keep choosing
senses.titleCN: 两人自愿维持的长期情谊
senses.definition: the warm, trusting relationship between people who choose each other's company
senses.definitionCN: 彼此选择对方作伴、相互信任的温暖关系
senses.example: Their friendship began in a shared dormitory and lasted fifty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的友谊始于同一间宿舍，持续了五十年。
senses.why: Old English built the word from friend plus -ship, a suffix for a state, so friendship is simply the condition of being friends.
senses.whyCN: 古英语用 friend 加表示状态的后缀构成这个词，因此友谊就是「作为朋友」的那种状态。

senses.title: The goodwill a friend carries
senses.definition: the affectionate goodwill that a friend feels and shows
senses.definitionCN: 朋友所怀有并表现出来的亲切善意
senses.example: He spoke of her with real friendship, not mere politeness.
senses.exampleCN: 他谈到她时带着真正的友情，而不只是客套。
senses.why: If friendship is a state, it can also be the feeling that maintains it, so the word names the warmth as well as the relation.
senses.whyCN: 如果说友谊是一种状态，它也可以指维持这种状态的情感，因此这个词既指关系，也指那份温情。

senses.title: The years a friendship lasts
senses.definition: the condition of being friends over a particular stretch of time
senses.definitionCN: 在某一特定时段内保持朋友关系的情形
senses.example: The friendship cooled after the business dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 那场生意纠纷之后，这份友谊冷了下来。
senses.why: The same noun covers the bond and its lifetime, since a relationship exists only as long as it is kept up.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既指情谊，也指它的存续期，因为关系只在被维持的期间内存在。

senses.title: Goodwill between groups or states
senses.titleCN: 团体或国家之间的友好关系
senses.definition: a cooperative relationship between organizations or countries that are not formally allied
senses.definitionCN: 未正式结盟的组织或国家之间的合作关系
senses.example: The two cities signed a friendship agreement in the town hall.
senses.exampleCN: 两座城市在市政厅签署了友好协议。
senses.why: Cities and states borrow the personal word for a link that is warmer than a treaty but less binding than an alliance.
senses.whyCN: 城市与国家借用这个私人词，指一种比条约更温和、比同盟更松散的联结。

senses.title: One friendship among many
senses.definition: a single instance of such a bond, countable and distinct from the rest
senses.definitionCN: 这种关系的一次具体实例，可数且与其余各段相区别
senses.example: She kept up friendships from every decade of her life.
senses.exampleCN: 她与人生每个十年里结识的朋友都保持着往来。
senses.why: Counting the word separates one particular bond from the general virtue, which is why the plural is so common.
senses.whyCN: 把词变成可数，就把某一段具体情谊与作为美德的友谊区分开来，因此复数形式极为常见。

senses.title: A link accepted on a screen
senses.titleCN: 社交平台上接受的好友关系
senses.definition: a connection accepted on a social platform that presents two users as friends
senses.definitionCN: 在社交平台上被接受、把两名用户呈现为好友的联结
senses.example: He accepted the friendship without ever meeting the man.
senses.exampleCN: 他接受了那条好友请求，却从未见过对方。
senses.why: Platforms needed a noun for the link itself, so they reused the oldest word for a bond and emptied it of time and trust.
senses.whyCN: 平台需要为这种联结找一个名词，于是动用了表示情谊的最古老的词，却抽掉了时间与信任。

senses.title: An alliance kept for advantage
senses.definition: a friendly arrangement maintained for gain rather than affection
senses.definitionCN: 出于得益而非情意维持的友好安排
senses.example: Their friendship was a friendship of convenience and both knew it.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的友情是彼此方便的结交，两边都心知肚明。
senses.why: Because the word promises trust, it can also be used ironically for a link that merely looks like trust.
senses.whyCN: 正因为这个词许诺信任，它也能反用来指一种只是看起来像信任的联结。

senses.title: Friendship as a thing to study
senses.titleCN: 被当作研究对象或德性的友谊
senses.definition: the virtue or social institution that philosophers and sociologists examine
senses.definitionCN: 哲学家与社会学家所考察的德性或社会制度
senses.example: The course reads ancient letters as evidence of how friendship was understood.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课把古代书信当作理解当时友谊观念的证据。
senses.why: Once a word names a relation, it can also name the thing itself as a topic, which is how friendship became a subject with a literature.
senses.whyCN: 一个词一旦指称某种关系，也能指称作为题目的事物本身，友谊由此成为有文献可查的课题。

intro.en: Friendship is an Old English compound of freond 'friend' and -scipe 'state, condition'. The noun for friend began as a participle of a verb meaning 'to love, to favour'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: friendship 是古英语复合词，由 freond「朋友」与 -scipe「状态、身份」构成。friend 最初是表示「爱、眷顾」的动词的分词。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: Freond 'friend' continues a Germanic participle meaning 'loving, favouring', from a verb reconstructed as frijon 'to love'. The verb form is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: freond「朋友」承自一个意为「爱着、眷顾着」的日耳曼语分词，其动词被重构为 frijon「爱」；该动词形式属重构，并非有记录的词。

items.en: -scipe meant 'state, condition, office' and is the same suffix heard in lordship and hardship; it names what a person or thing is, not what they do.
items.cn: -scipe 意为「状态、身份、职位」，与 lordship、hardship 中的后缀相同；它指人或物「是什么」，而非「做什么」。

items.en: The compound is recorded in Old English for friendship or favour, but no single earliest citation can be dated precisely.
items.cn: 这一复合词在古英语中已用来指友谊或眷顾，但没有哪一条最早书证能定出确切年代。

items.en: Middle English carried the word through changes of spelling without changing its sense, and it remained the ordinary noun for the bond between friends.
items.cn: 中古英语在拼写变化中沿用这个词，词义未变，它始终是表示朋友间情谊的常用名词。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): the Germanic verb behind friend is reconstructed, its Indo-European ancestor is likewise a reconstruction, and the earliest Old English citation is not fixed with confidence.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与首见年代）：friend 背后的日耳曼语动词属重构，其印欧祖形同样是重构，古英语最早书证也无法确定年份。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root family and one near neighbour of a different root that is often mistaken for a relative; group two holds the words that describe closeness between people.
note.cn: 第一组是同根词族，外加一个常被误认作同族、实则不同源的近形词；第二组是描述人际亲近的近似词。

entries.definition: The noun inside the compound; it names the person, while friendship names the relationship between two such people.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词中的名词部分；它指人，而 friendship 指两个这样的人之间的关系。

entries.definition: The adjective built on friend with the old suffix for 'having the form of'; it describes behaviour, not the bond itself.
entries.definitionCN: 由 friend 加表示「具有……形态」的旧后缀构成的形容词；它描述行为，而非关系本身。

entries.definition: Old English feond meant 'enemy'; the shape is close to friend but the roots are unrelated, which is why the pair is a trap.
entries.definitionCN: 古英语 feond 意为「敌人」；字形与 friend 相近，词根却毫无关系，因此这一对极易误认。

entries.definition: Un- plus friend, formed in the age of social platforms for removing a name from a list; it is not an old word.
entries.definitionCN: 由 un- 加 friend，在社交平台时代才出现，指把某人移出好友名单；它不是古老词。

entries.definition: The state of having someone beside you; it stresses presence and shared hours rather than the affection friendship implies.
entries.definitionCN: 身边有人的状态；它强调在场与共处的时间，而非 friendship 所含的情意。

entries.definition: The closeness of people who work or fight together; it rests on a common task, while friendship rests on choice.
entries.definitionCN: 一同工作或战斗的人之间的亲近；它依托共同任务，而友谊依托彼此选择。

entries.definition: Any strong link between people, including family and colleagues; it is broader and often more physical in feel.
entries.definitionCN: 人与人之间的任何强烈联结，包括家人与同事；含义更宽，感觉上常更具体。

entries.definition: A formal union of parties for a purpose; it is political or strategic, and carries none of the warmth of friendship.
entries.definitionCN: 各方为某目的结成的正式联合；它是政治或策略性的，不含友谊的温情。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Old English parts, the real suffix family and the real verbs that pair with the noun.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实存在的古英语构词成分、真实的后缀词族，以及真实与这个名词搭配的动词。

normal.en: The suffix is the one heard in lordship and hardship: a state or condition, here the state of being a friend.
normal.cn: 这个后缀也出现在 lordship 与 hardship 中：表状态或身份，此处即「身为朋友」的状态。

normal.en: Friend began as a participle meaning 'loving', so friendship is literally the condition of one who loves.
normal.cn: friend 原为意为「爱着」的分词，所以友谊字面上就是「爱着的人所处的状态」。

normal.en: The noun takes real verbs: form a friendship, strike up a friendship, keep up a friendship, break off a friendship.
normal.cn: 这个名词有真实动词搭配：建立友谊、结下友谊、维持友谊、断绝友谊。

normal.en: Its adjective is friendly and its abstract quality is friendliness, both built with ordinary English endings.
normal.cn: 它的形容词是 friendly，抽象性质是 friendliness，两者都用普通英语词尾构成。

normal.en: Companionship is the nearest rival, but it counts hours together, while friendship counts affection.
normal.cn: 最接近的是 companionship，但它算的是共处的时间，而 friendship 算的是情意。

abstract.en: Picture a vine crossing a wall because two children planted the same seed on both sides.
abstract.cn: 想象一株藤蔓翻过院墙，因为两个孩子在墙两边种下了同一颗种子。

abstract.en: Picture two chairs left outside overnight, neither moved, both damp with the same rain.
abstract.cn: 想象两把椅子整夜放在户外，谁也没搬动，被同一场雨同时打湿。

abstract.en: Picture a debt between two people that neither of them ever tries to settle.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人之间的一笔账，谁也从不去结清。

examples.en: Their friendship survived a year of silence and two arguments about money.
examples.cn: 他们的友谊熬过了一年的沉默与两次关于钱的争吵。

examples.en: The school pairs older pupils with younger ones to build friendships across year groups.
examples.cn: 学校让高年级学生与低年级学生结对，以跨年级建立友谊。

examples.en: The two ports have kept a friendship agreement since the war ended.
examples.cn: 战争结束后，两座港口城市一直维持着友好协议。

root: 古英语 freond「朋友」+ -scipe「状态、身份」；freond 原为「爱、眷顾」动词的分词，该日耳曼语动词与印欧祖形均属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one chosen bond: two people keep choosing each other, the goodwill they carry, the years it lasts, the goodwill between cities, single instances of it, a link accepted on a screen, a bargain dressed as affection, and the thing philosophers study.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一份自愿的情谊展开：两人不断重新选择对方、心中所怀的善意、情谊存续的岁月、城市之间的友好、若干段中的一段、屏幕上接受的联结、披着情意的利益结交，最后是被当作课题来研究的友谊。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vine grown from one seed on two sides of a wall, never cut where it crosses.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗种子在墙两边长出的同一株藤，越过墙头处从未被剪断。

branches.en: PERSONAL BOND IN TIME: the relationship itself and the stretch of years through which it is kept up.
branches.cn: 私人情谊及其岁月：关系本身，以及维持这段关系的那些年头。

branches.en: THE FEELING INSIDE IT: goodwill is what keeps the state alive from day to day.
branches.cn: 关系中的情感：善意是让这种状态逐日存活的东西。

branches.en: BETWEEN BODIES: cities and states borrow the personal word for cooperation without a treaty.
branches.cn: 团体之间：城市与国家借用这个私人词，指不签条约的合作。

branches.en: COUNTED AND BARGAINED: one friendship among many, and the ironic version kept only for advantage.
branches.cn: 可数者与交易者：若干段中的一段，以及只为利益而维持的那种反用。

branches.en: SCREEN AND STUDY: a link emptied of time, and the bond turned into a subject with a literature.
branches.cn: 屏幕与学问：被抽掉时间的联结，以及成为有文献之课题的情谊。

intro.en: Friendship is a Germanic compound whose two parts still work separately in English, so the whole family reads clearly.
intro.cn: friendship 是日耳曼语复合词，两部分在英语中仍各自独立运作，因此整个词族都能读得清楚。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin root: friend and -ship are both Germanic, and the suffix is still productive in modern English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根：friend 与 -ship 都属日耳曼语，而这个后缀在现代英语中仍有构词能力。

senses.definition: sound arranged in rhythm and melody, made by voices or instruments and valued as an art
senses.definitionCN: 按节奏与旋律安排、由人声或乐器发出并被当作艺术的声音
senses.example: She studied music at the conservatory for four years.
senses.exampleCN: 她在音乐学院学了四年音乐。
senses.why: Greek mousike named the work of the Muses, so the word starts as a disciplined craft rather than as any noise that happens to be loud.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 mousikē 原本指缪斯所掌管的技艺，所以这个词的起点是「有章法的技艺」，而不是碰巧很响的杂音。

senses.title: A piece or a body of written works
senses.definition: a particular composition, or the whole set of pieces written by one composer or within one style
senses.definitionCN: 某一首具体的作品，或某位作曲家、某种风格写下的全部作品
senses.example: The orchestra played music by Ravel and Debussy.
senses.exampleCN: 管弦乐队演奏了拉威尔与德彪西的作品。
senses.why: Because one noun can name both the art and the things made by that art, music also points to individual pieces you can put on a programme.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既能指这门艺术，也能指它做出的东西，因此 music 又可以指可以排进节目单的一首首具体作品。

senses.title: The sound actually heard in performance
senses.definition: the audible sound that reaches the ear when instruments or voices are playing
senses.definitionCN: 乐器或人声演奏时真正传到耳朵里的声音
senses.example: From the next room came the music of a violin.
senses.exampleCN: 隔壁房间传来小提琴的乐声。
senses.why: The abstract art becomes audible only at the moment of playing, so the same noun also names the physical sound filling the room.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的艺术只有在演奏的那一刻才变得可听，于是同一个名词也用来指充满房间的实际声响。

senses.title: Music laid under a film, game or ceremony
senses.definition: music used behind another activity to support its mood or mark its moments
senses.definitionCN: 垫在另一项活动之下、用来烘托气氛或标记节点的音乐
senses.example: The film's music does most of the emotional work.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片的情绪多半由配乐承担。
senses.why: Once music is thought of as a layer under something else, the word takes the role of accompaniment, from cinema to a graduation ceremony.
senses.whyCN: 当音乐被看成垫在别的东西下面的一层，这个词就承担了伴奏的角色，从电影到毕业典礼都是如此。

intro.en: Music reaches English from the Greek art of the Muses by way of Latin and French, and its meaning widened from one craft to works, sound and accompaniment.
intro.cn: music 从希腊语中「缪斯的技艺」出发，经拉丁语与法语进入英语，词义也从一门技艺扩展到作品、声响与伴奏。

items.en: Mousike was the art presided over by the Muses and covered poetry, song and dance rather than instrumental playing alone.
items.cn: mousikē 是缪斯掌管的技艺，包括诗歌、歌唱与舞蹈，并不只指器乐演奏。

items.en: Latin took the word as musica and used it for the art of sound, one of the disciplines of the medieval schools.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个词写作 musica，用来指声音的艺术，是中世纪学校里的学科之一。

items.en: Old French musique carried the word into everyday use for music and for the notation that records it.
items.cn: 古法语 musique 把这个词带入日常使用，既指音乐，也指记录音乐的谱子。

items.en: Middle English music named both the art and a written score, and the two meanings stayed side by side for centuries.
items.cn: 中古英语的 music 同时指这门艺术和一份写下的乐谱，两个含义并行了数百年。

items.en: Modern English adds the performed sound and the music written for films and ceremonies, so one word covers art, work, sound and setting.
items.cn: 现代英语又加上演奏出来的声响以及为电影、典礼写的配乐，一个词于是覆盖艺术、作品、声音与场景四层。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the forms built on this stem; the near-meaning group collects the things a piece of music is made of.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个词干构成的同族形式；近义组收构成一段音乐的基本元素。

entries.definition: The adjective built on music with -al, meaning of music or sounding pleasant.
entries.definitionCN: 由 music 加 -al 构成的形容词，义为「音乐的」或「悦耳的」。

entries.definition: The person noun built on music with -ian, meaning one who plays or writes music.
entries.definitionCN: 由 music 加 -ian 构成的名词，指演奏或创作音乐的人。

entries.definition: The skill of a musician, formed by adding -ship to musician.
entries.definitionCN: 在 musician 后加 -ship 构成，指音乐家的演奏修养。

entries.definition: The adverb from musical, meaning in a way connected with music.
entries.definitionCN: 由 musical 派生出的副词，义为「在音乐方面」。

entries.definition: The sequence of notes that carries a tune.
entries.definitionCN: 承载曲调的连续音。

entries.definition: A short melody you can hum or whistle.
entries.definitionCN: 可以哼唱或吹出的短曲调。

entries.definition: A piece meant to be sung, words and music together.
entries.definitionCN: 为歌唱而作的作品，词与曲合一。

normalIntro.en: The word is the base of a small family, and the family shows how one noun grows an adjective, a person and a quality.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一小族词的基干，这一族词演示了一个名词如何长出形容词、人物名词和抽象品质。

normal.en: Music is the base of the family: add -al for the adjective musical, add -ian for the person musician.
normal.cn: music 是这一族词的基干：加 -al 得到形容词 musical，加 -ian 得到表示人的 musician。

normal.en: The Greek source mousike meant the art of the Muses, and museum comes from the same shrine, so the two words began as neighbours.
normal.cn: 希腊语 mousikē 意为缪斯的技艺，museum 也出自缪斯的神庙，两个词在源头上是邻居。

normal.en: Music is uncountable, so you say a piece of music or a lot of music, never a music.
normal.cn: music 不可数，所以要说 a piece of music 或 a lot of music，不能说 a music。

normal.en: Sheet music is the written notes rather than the sound, which is why the phrase turns up in every score shop.
normal.cn: sheet music 指纸上写下的音符而不是声响，所以这个说法总出现在卖乐谱的地方。

normal.en: Music to my ears is a fixed idiom for news that makes you glad to hear it.
normal.cn: music to my ears 是固定习语，指让人听了高兴的消息。

abstract.en: Picture the hush in a hall just before the conductor raises a hand: music is what fills that silence on purpose.
abstract.cn: 想象音乐厅里指挥抬手前的那片安静：音乐就是有意填满这片安静的东西。

abstract.en: One noun covering art, works and background sound shows how deeply music is layered into ordinary days.
abstract.cn: 一个名词同时覆盖艺术、作品与背景声音，说明音乐早已层层嵌进平常的日子。

abstract.en: If you can hum it, it is already music, even before anyone writes it down.
abstract.cn: 只要你能把它哼出来，它就已经是音乐，哪怕还没有人把它记下来。

examples.en: She writes music for films and games.
examples.cn: 她为电影和游戏作曲。

examples.en: The music was so loud that we could feel the bass through the floor.
examples.cn: 音乐声太大，隔着地板都能感到低音的震动。

examples.en: He stood listening to the music of a street violinist.
examples.cn: 他站着听一位街头小提琴手的琴声。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「缪齐克」：缪斯女神一抬手，音乐就响了；记住 music 是音乐。

root: 一般认为来自希腊语 mousikē（缪斯的技艺），经拉丁语 musica、古法语 musique 进入英语；同族词围绕「音乐」与「做音乐的人」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is organized sound valued as an art; from it the word reaches the works themselves, the sound heard while playing, and music placed under another activity.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被当作艺术的有序声音；由此分出具体的作品、演奏时听到的声响，以及垫在别的活动之下的配乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bow crossing a string and turning silence into ordered sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：琴弓划过琴弦，把寂静变成有秩序的声响。

branches.en: a practice room where scales slowly become a piece
branches.cn: 琴房里音阶慢慢连成一首曲子

branches.en: a shelf of scores filed under one composer's name
branches.cn: 按一位作曲家名字归档的一架乐谱

branches.en: an orchestra reading a new score for the first time
branches.cn: 乐团第一次读一份新总谱

branches.en: a violin's sound reaching the room next door
branches.cn: 小提琴的声音传到隔壁房间

branches.en: a soundtrack swelling under a closing scene
branches.cn: 片尾画面下渐渐涨起的配乐

intro.en: The family is built on the noun music plus two suffixes: -al for the adjective and -ian for the person, with Latin musica underneath all of them.
intro.cn: 这一族词建立在名词 music 之上，再加 -al 构成形容词、加 -ian 构成指人的名词，底下则是拉丁语 musica。

latinIntro.en: Latin musica came from Greek mousike and became the medieval European word for the art of sound.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 musica 来自希腊语 mousikē，后来成为中世纪欧洲指「声音的艺术」的词。

definition_en: words or a message that show you are happy about someone's good luck or success
core_image: 拍着肩膀说出的那句「你真棒」
scene: 比赛结果公布，同学们围着获奖的选手说个不停。 He received a card full of congratulation after winning the race.
sceneCN: 这里 congratulation 是「祝贺」（第 1 个义项：表达高兴的话语）；句意是他赛跑获胜后收到写满祝贺的卡片。

derivatives.zh: congratulation 的动词形式，义为「祝贺；向…道贺」
由 congratulation 加 -ory 构成，义为「祝贺的」

senses.title: Words showing joy at someone's success
senses.definition: kind words said when someone succeeds or has good luck
senses.definitionCN: 他人成功或交好运时说的暖心话
senses.example: Congratulations on winning the writing contest!
senses.exampleCN: 恭喜你赢得作文比赛！
senses.why: The Latin root gratus means pleasing: you show that another's joy pleases you too.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 gratus 意为令人高兴：表明对方的喜事也让你高兴。

senses.title: A message or card of praise
senses.definition: a written message or card giving such kind words
senses.definitionCN: 写有祝贺话语的信件或卡片
senses.example: The class wrote congratulation cards for the retiring teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 全班为退休老师写贺卡。
senses.why: Spoken joy can be put on paper and sent.
senses.whyCN: 口头的高兴可以落到纸上寄出去。

senses.title: The act of expressing joy to someone
senses.definition: the action of telling someone you are pleased for them
senses.definitionCN: 向他人表达高兴之情的举动
senses.example: Their warm congratulation made the shy winner smile.
senses.exampleCN: 他们热情的祝贺让腼腆的获奖者露出了笑容。
senses.why: The message becomes the act itself in daily use.
senses.whyCN: 日常用法中，贺词与祝贺行为合二为一。

intro.en: Congratulation is built on Latin words for wishing joy.
intro.cn: congratulation 建立在拉丁语「祝喜」的词根之上。

items.en: Latin gratus meant pleasing or thankful, seen in grateful.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gratus 意为令人高兴的、感恩的，见于 grateful。

items.en: Latin congratulari meant to wish joy to someone together.
items.cn: 拉丁语 congratulari 意为与他人一同表示喜悦。

items.en: Late Latin congratulatio named the act of wishing joy.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 congratulatio 指致贺这一行为。

items.en: Middle English congratulacion appeared in formal letters of praise.
items.cn: 中古英语 congratulacion 出现在正式贺信中。

items.en: Modern English congratulations became the everyday cheer of success.
items.cn: 现代英语 congratulations 成为日常道贺用语。

examples.en: She sent a congratulation card to her pen friend abroad.

senses.exampleCN: 我们七点坐下来安静地吃了一顿饭。
senses.why: Old English mǣl first meant a measured or appointed time, so a meal was originally the hour set aside for eating rather than the food itself.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 mǣl 本指量好、约定的时间，所以 meal 最初是吃饭被安排的那个时刻，而不是食物本身。

senses.title: The food eaten at such an occasion
senses.definition: the food that is served and eaten at one sitting
senses.definitionCN: 一次坐下用餐时所端上并被吃掉的食物
senses.example: She cooked a simple meal of rice and vegetables.
senses.exampleCN: 她做了一顿简单的米饭加蔬菜。
senses.why: Once the appointed hour had a name, the word slid from the time to what filled that time, namely the food on the table.
senses.whyCN: 一旦那个约定的时刻有了名字，词义就从时间滑向填满这段时间的东西，也就是桌上的食物。

senses.title: Grain ground into coarse powder
senses.definition: grain, especially oats or corn, ground coarsely rather than into fine flour
senses.definitionCN: 尤指燕麦或玉米磨得较粗、而非磨成细面粉的谷物
senses.example: The mill turns oats into meal for the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 磨坊把燕麦磨成粗粉，留着过冬。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different Old English word, melu, meaning flour; the two words fell together in spelling and now share one entry.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项来自另一个古英语词 melu，意为面粉；两个词在拼写上合流，如今共用一个词条。

senses.title: Any coarsely ground product used as feed or fertilizer
senses.definition: a powdered product made by grinding bones, fish or shells, used as animal feed or fertilizer
senses.definitionCN: 把骨头、鱼或贝壳磨成粉、用作饲料或肥料的产品
senses.example: Bone meal is spread on the field before planting.
senses.exampleCN: 种植前把骨粉撒在田里。
senses.why: The grinding image at the heart of the flour sense extends easily to bones, fish and shells once industry needs a word for powdered additives.
senses.whyCN: 面粉义项核心的「磨碎」意象很容易延伸到骨头、鱼和贝壳，只要工业需要一个词来称粉末状的添加物。

intro.en: Meal is two Old English words that look alike today: one for an appointed time, one for ground grain.
intro.cn: meal 其实是两个古英语词，今天看起来一样：一个指约定的时间，一个指磨碎的谷物。

items.en: The noun *mēlą meant a measure or a marked point of time, and it is the ancestor of the repast sense.
items.cn: 名词 *mēlą 意为尺度或标出的时间点，是「一餐」这一义项的祖先。

items.en: Old English mǣl named an appointed time and later the meal eaten at that time.
items.cn: 古英语 mǣl 指约定的时刻，后来也指那个时刻吃的那顿饭。

items.en: A separate word, melu, meant flour or grain ground fine, and it is the ancestor of the powder sense.
items.cn: 另一个词 melu 意为面粉或磨细的谷物，是「粗粉」义项的祖先。

items.en: Middle English spelled both words close to mele, and they gradually merged into one form.
items.cn: 中古英语把两个词都写成接近 mele 的形式，二者逐渐合并成一个词形。

items.en: Modern English keeps both senses in one entry and builds compounds such as oatmeal and cornmeal.
items.cn: 现代英语把两个义项收在同一词条里，并构成 oatmeal、cornmeal 等复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the powder family and its mill; the near-meaning group gathers words for a sitting at the table and for ground grain.
note.cn: 形近组收「粉」这一族词和它的磨坊；近义组收表示围桌用餐的词与表示磨碎谷物的词。

entries.definition: Like meal or covered with meal; also used of dry, pale food.
entries.definitionCN: 像粗粉的、覆着粉的；也形容食物干而发白。

entries.definition: The time when a meal is normally eaten.
entries.definitionCN: 通常吃饭的时间。

entries.definition: Oats ground into meal, or the porridge made from them.
entries.definitionCN: 燕麦磨成的粗粉，或由此煮成的粥。

entries.definition: A building or machine that grinds grain.
entries.definitionCN: 磨谷的厂房或机器；磨坊。

entries.definition: The main meal of the day, usually in the evening.
entries.definitionCN: 一天中的正餐，通常指晚餐。

entries.definition: A meal, especially a formal or leisurely one.
entries.definitionCN: 一餐，尤指正式或从容的一顿。

entries.definition: A small amount of food eaten between meals.
entries.definitionCN: 两餐之间吃的一点食物。

entries.definition: Fine powder made by grinding grain, finer than meal.
entries.definitionCN: 谷物磨成的细粉，比粗粉更细。

normalIntro.en: One spelling now holds two histories: a measured hour and a handful of ground grain.
normalIntro.cn: 同一个拼写如今装着两段历史：量出的时刻与一把磨碎的谷物。

normal.en: Old English mǣl meant an appointed time, so the earliest meal was a moment on the clock rather than a plate of food.
normal.cn: 古英语 mǣl 意为约定的时刻，所以最早的 meal 是钟表上的一个时刻，而不是一盘食物。

normal.en: The flour sense comes from melu, a different Old English word that later merged with mǣl in spelling.
normal.cn: 「粉」的义项来自 melu，一个后来在拼写上并入 mǣl 的另一个古英语词。

normal.en: Mealtime and oatmeal are compounds: one adds time, the other adds the grain that was ground.
normal.cn: mealtime 与 oatmeal 都是复合词：一个加上时间，一个加上被磨碎的谷物。

normal.en: The adjective mealy adds -y to meal, giving the idea of something powdery on the surface.
normal.cn: 形容词 mealy 在 meal 后加 -y，表示表面有粉末状的东西。

normal.en: Cornmeal and oatmeal keep the old powder sense alive in kitchens today.
normal.cn: cornmeal 与 oatmeal 让古老的粉末义项至今仍活在厨房里。

abstract.en: A meal is a clock and a table at once: time measured out, then filled with food.
abstract.cn: 一餐既是钟也是桌：先把时间量出来，再用食物把它填满。

abstract.en: Two words that once meant different things can end up spelled the same, and a dictionary entry quietly holds both.
abstract.cn: 两个原本意思不同的词可能最终拼写相同，而一个词条会安静地把二者都收下。

abstract.en: Grinding turns hard grain into soft powder, which is why the same word can name a dinner and a bag of feed.
abstract.cn: 磨碎把坚硬的谷物变成软粉，所以同一个词既能称一顿饭，也能称一袋饲料。

examples.en: We usually have a quiet meal before the school bus arrives.
examples.cn: 校车到来之前，我们通常安静地吃一顿饭。

examples.en: She cooked a simple meal of rice and vegetables.
examples.cn: 她做了一顿简单的米饭加蔬菜。

examples.en: The old mill still grinds corn into meal.
examples.cn: 那座老磨坊仍把玉米磨成粗粉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米了」——米下锅了，就该吃饭；记住 meal 是一餐，也是磨出来的粗粉。

root: 表示「一餐」的义项来自古英语 mǣl（约定的时刻），出自原始日耳曼语 *mēlą；表示「粗粉」的义项来自古英语 melu（面粉），与 mill 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is food at a set time; the senses then split between the occasion, the food, the ground grain and industrial powders.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是按时吃的那顿饭；义项由此分成吃饭的场合、食物本身、磨碎的谷物与工业粗粉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bowl on a wooden table beside a sack of ground grain.
core.cn: 核心意象：木桌上一只碗，旁边是一袋磨好的谷物粉。

branches.en: a clock marking the hour set aside for eating
branches.cn: 钟表指向专门留给吃饭的时刻

branches.en: a table filled with rice and vegetables
branches.cn: 摆着米饭和蔬菜的饭桌

branches.en: oats falling from the millstone into a sack
bone meal scattered across a field
a family arriving and sitting down together
branches.cn: 一家人到齐后一起坐下

intro.en: The entry is held together by a Germanic time word, a Germanic flour word, and a handful of English compounds and suffixes.
intro.cn: 这个词条由日耳曼语的时间词、日耳曼语的面粉词，以及若干英语复合词与后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Neither Germanic word behind meal has a reliable Latin cognate; Latin molere belongs to the grinding family but is not the source of this word.
latinIntro.cn: meal 背后的两个日耳曼词都没有可靠的拉丁同族词；拉丁语 molere 属「磨」的词族，却不是这个词的来源。

definition_en: a colored liquid used for writing, printing or drawing
core_image: 钢笔尖滴下的深色液体
scene: 书房里钢笔在纸上沙沙作响。 The artist drew the cat in black ink.
sceneCN: 这里 ink 是「墨水」（第 1 个义项：书写用液体）；句意：画家用黑墨水画那只猫。

derivatives.zh: ink 加形容词后缀，义为「墨黑的；沾满墨水的」
ink 加 well 复合，义为「墨水池」
ink 加 pad 复合，义为「印台」

senses.title: Liquid for writing
senses.definition: colored liquid used for writing or drawing
senses.definitionCN: 用于书写或绘画的带色液体
senses.example: Sign the form in ink, not pencil.
senses.exampleCN: 请用墨水而非铅笔签名。
senses.why: The pen drinks black blood from the bottle.
senses.whyCN: 钢笔从瓶里喝下黑色的血。

senses.title: Printing fluid
senses.definition: liquid used by printing machines
senses.definitionCN: 印刷机使用的液体
senses.example: The news smelled of fresh ink.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸散发着新油墨的气味。
senses.why: The same liquid feeds the roller.
senses.whyCN: 同样的液体喂给滚筒。

senses.title: Money made, in accounting
senses.definition: black ink means profit in account books
senses.definitionCN: 账簿上黑墨代表盈利
senses.example: The store finally ran in black ink.
senses.exampleCN: 店铺终于实现了盈利。
senses.why: The bookkeeper's pen decides the color of fate.
senses.whyCN: 账房先生的笔决定命运的颜色。

senses.title: To sign or fill with ink
senses.definition: to sign or mark something with ink
senses.definitionCN: 用墨水签署或标记
senses.example: Both teams inked the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 双方签署了合同。
senses.why: The pen is dipped and pressed down on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 笔尖蘸墨，被刻意按下。

intro.en: Ink comes from Old French encre, from Late Latin encaustum, from Greek enkauston, something burned in. Purple ink was fixed with fire, like encaustic painting.
intro.cn: ink 来自古法语 encre，源自晚期拉丁语 encaustum，再溯源至希腊语 enkauston「以火烧定之物」。紫色墨水曾像蜡画一样用火固定。

items.en: Greek enkaiein meant to burn in; enkauston named fire-fixed paint.
items.cn: 希腊语 enkaiein 意为烧入；enkauston 指以火固定的颜料。

items.en: Late Latin encaustum named the imperial purple ink.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 encaustum 指帝国的紫色墨水。

items.en: Old French encre shortened the word as it traveled west.
items.cn: 古法语 encre 在西传途中缩短了词形。

items.en: Middle English enke or inke settled the spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语 enke/inke 确定了拼写。

items.en: Modern English added the verb sense and the business color code of red and black.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了动词义与账面上红黑两色的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the ink family and its neighbors. The meaning group compares words of writing fluids.
note.cn: 形近组收录 ink 词族与相邻词；词义组比较书写用液的词。

entries.definition: black as ink.

entries.definition: the little bottle in old desks.
entries.definitionCN: 旧书桌上的小墨水瓶。

entries.definition: a color; one letter apart.
entries.definitionCN: 粉色；只差一个字母。

entries.definition: colored liquid for surfaces.
entries.definitionCN: 涂于表面的有色液体。

entries.definition: coloring liquid for cloth or hair.
entries.definitionCN: 给布或头发上色的液体。

entries.definition: the dry color powder before liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 调液之前的干色粉。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the burn origin, the in-ink rule and the red-black accounts.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩利用「火烧」词源、in ink 规则与红黑账目。

normal.en: Greek enkauston: ink was once fixed with fire.
normal.cn: 希腊语 enkauston：墨水曾用火固定。

normal.en: write in ink is the fixed pattern.
normal.cn: write in ink 是固定搭配。

normal.en: red ink is loss; black ink is profit.
normal.cn: red ink 是亏损，black ink 是盈利。

normal.en: inky describes fingers after a leaky pen.
normal.cn: inky 形容钢笔漏水后的手指。

normal.en: inked the contract is sports slang for signing.
normal.cn: inked the contract 是签约的体育俚语。

abstract.en: One image: a bottle of black blood for pens.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：一瓶给钢笔喝的黑血。

abstract.en: Ink is fire tamed into writing.
abstract.cn: ink 是被驯服进书写的火。

abstract.en: Every signature leaves a small dark wound on paper.
abstract.cn: 每个签名都在纸上留下小小的黑痕。

examples.en: Please fill in the form in blue ink.
examples.cn: 请用蓝墨水填表。

examples.en: An ink stain spread across the page.
examples.cn: 墨渍在纸上洇开。

examples.en: The company was finally in black ink.
examples.cn: 公司终于扭亏为盈。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「应刻」：墨水应刻在纸上留下痕迹， ink。

root: 希腊语 enkaiein「烧入」→ enkauston「火烧固定的颜料」→ 晚期拉丁语 encaustum「紫色墨水」→ 古法语 encre → 中古英语 enke/inke → 现代英语 ink。

sensesIntro.en: Ink is bottled dark blood: for the pen, the press, the account book, and the contract waiting to be signed.
sensesIntro.cn: ink 是瓶装的黑血：喂钢笔、喂印刷机、写进账本，以及按在待签的合同上。

core.en: Dark liquid that carries words, pictures and even profit.

definition_zh: 两倍的；加倍的；双人的；翻倍；对折
definition_en: twice as much or as many, or to make something twice as large
core_image: 两张一模一样的纸叠在一起
scene: 运动会上，接力赛最后一棒冲线，全场分数翻了番。 Sales doubled after the shop opened a second floor.
sceneCN: 这里 double 是「翻倍」（第 2 个义项：变成两倍）；句意：商店开了二楼后，销售额翻了一番。

derivatives.zh: double 加指小后缀构成，义为「紧身衣；（语言学）同源对偶词」
double 加副词后缀构成，义为「加倍地」
double 的动名词，义为「加倍；对折」

senses.title: Twice as much or as many
senses.definition: being twice the size, number, or amount
senses.definitionCN: 大小、数量或程度是两倍
senses.example: She paid double the usual price.
senses.exampleCN: 她付了平时两倍的价钱。
senses.why: Latin duplus means twofold: one folded thing laid on another makes the pair image.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 duplus 意为「两层的」：一物对折压在另一物上，便有了成对的画面。

senses.title: To become twice as large
senses.definition: to become twice as much or as many
senses.definitionCN: 变成原来的两倍
senses.example: The village doubled in size in ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 十年间村子规模翻了一番。
senses.why: If a thing doubles, the pair image grows: one becomes two without cutting.
senses.whyCN: 东西翻倍时，成对的画面长大：一变成二，无需切分。

senses.title: Made for two people
senses.definition: made for or holding two persons
senses.definitionCN: 供两人使用或容纳两人
senses.example: They booked a double room by the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在海边订了一间双人房。
senses.why: The pair of sheets becomes a pair of sleepers: two of the same share one thing.
senses.whyCN: 成对的东西变成成对的人：两个相同者共享一件事物。

senses.title: To bend or fold over
senses.definition: to bend something so one part lies on another
senses.definitionCN: 把某物折弯使一部分压在另一部分上
senses.example: He doubled the paper and put it in his pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 他把纸对折后放进口袋。
senses.why: The original folding action survives in paper and cloth.
senses.whyCN: 最初的对折动作在纸与布上留存了下来。

senses.title: To show the way
senses.definition: to lead a person or animal along a route
senses.definitionCN: 带领人或动物沿某条路线前进
senses.example: She guided the visitors to the exit.
senses.exampleCN: 她把参观者引到出口。
senses.why: The flag holder walks first, so the verb begins as physically leading the road.
senses.whyCN: 画面是举旗的人走在最前，动词最初就是实实在在的带路。

senses.title: To help control movement
senses.definition: to help something move in the right direction
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某物沿正确方向移动
senses.example: He guided the car into the narrow space.
senses.exampleCN: 他把车缓缓开进狭窄的车位。
senses.why: Hands on a wheel guide as much as feet on a path; direction-keeping is the shared idea.
senses.whyCN: 握方向盘与走路线同属「保持方向」，画面从脚步扩展到操控。

senses.title: A person who leads visitors
senses.definition: someone whose job is to show visitors around a place
senses.definitionCN: 以带游客参观为职业的人
senses.example: Our guide spoke three languages.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的导游会说三种语言。
senses.why: The one who walks ahead gets a name, turning the action into a job title.
senses.whyCN: 走在前面的人获得称呼，动作变成职业名。

senses.title: A book of instructions
senses.definition: a book or document that explains how to do or understand something
senses.definitionCN: 讲解如何做事或理解某物的书册
senses.example: Read the user guide before starting the machine.
senses.exampleCN: 开机前先读用户手册。
senses.why: A silent book can lead too; pages replace the walking leader.
senses.whyCN: 书也能带路，纸页代替了走在前面的人。

senses.title: Something that shapes decisions
senses.definition: a rule, feeling, or example that influences choices
senses.definitionCN: 影响决策的规则、感觉或榜样
senses.example: Her honesty is a guide for the whole class.
senses.exampleCN: 她的诚实是全班学习的榜样。
senses.why: Direction can be moral; the inner compass extends the leading image to choices.
senses.whyCN: 方向感也可以是道德的，内心指南针把「带路」延伸到抉择。

intro.en: Guide comes through French from a Germanic word about watching and showing the road.
intro.cn: guide 经古法语来自日耳曼语词，与「看路、指路」有关。

items.en: A Frankish root witan meant to show the way, related to words for watching.
items.cn: 法兰克语词根 witan 意为指路，与「看」类词相关。

items.en: Old French guider meant to lead or guide, borrowing the Germanic root.
items.cn: 古法语 guider 意为引导、带路，借自日耳曼词根。

items.en: Occitan forms helped carry the word across into northern French before English met it.
items.cn: 奥克语形式帮助该词传入北部法语，随后与英语相遇。（存疑关联）

items.en: Middle English borrowed gide or guide in the fourteenth century for both leading and advising.
items.cn: 十四世纪中古英语借入 guide，兼指带路与劝导。

items.en: Modern English added guidebooks, user guides, and the moral sense of a guiding principle.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了指南书、用户手册以及「指导原则」的道德义。

examples.en: A good guide makes history come alive.

examples.en: Parents guide children not by commands but by examples.
examples.cn: 父母以身作则而非命令来引导孩子。

definition_en: the head of a state, a university, a company, or a meeting, especially one chosen to lead and to preside over others
core_image: 一张长桌的尽头，一个人坐在最前面的椅子上，所有人的目光都朝他那边
scene: 长桌两侧坐满了人，争论停不下来，最后大家都看向尽头那把椅子，等坐在那里的人开口。 The president of the club called for a vote.
sceneCN: 这里 president 指「会长、会议主席」（第 4 个义项：被推举出来主持会议的人）；句意为俱乐部会长要求进行表决。图中可辨识物件：长桌、成排的椅子、举起的手。

collocations.phrase: the president of the United States

derivatives.zh: 由 president 换后缀 -cy 构成，义为「总统职位；任期」
由 president 加 -ial 构成，义为「总统的；总统制的」
与 president 同出拉丁 praesidere，义为「主持；担任主席」

senses.title: The head of a state
senses.definition: the elected head of a republic, who leads the government and represents the country
senses.definitionCN: 共和国的民选元首，领导政府并代表国家
senses.example: The president addressed the nation on television.
senses.exampleCN: 总统通过电视向全国发表讲话。
senses.why: The Latin source means to sit in front, and the leader of a state is pictured as the person seated at the head of the table where decisions are made.
senses.whyCN: 词源本义是「坐在前面」，国家领导人正被想象成长桌首位上坐着的人，所有决定都从他那里发出，因此「总统」是这个坐前意象在政治上的放大。

senses.title: The head of a university
senses.definition: the senior officer who leads a university or a college
senses.definitionCN: 领导一所大学或学院的最高负责人
senses.example: The president welcomed the new students at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 校长在校门口迎接新生。
senses.why: A university is also a body with a council and a hall, so its leader inherits the same image of the person who sits before the assembly and speaks for it.
senses.whyCN: 大学同样有校务会议与礼堂，它的负责人也就继承了同一幅画面：坐在众人之前、代表整个机构讲话的人，于是这个词从国家元首平移到校长。

senses.title: The head of a company
senses.definition: the most senior officer of a company or organization
senses.definitionCN: 公司或机构中职位最高的负责人
senses.example: The president of the firm signed the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 公司董事长签署了这份合同。
senses.why: Boards meet around a table, and the officer who sits at its head and signs for the company keeps the literal seating arrangement inside the modern title.
senses.whyCN: 董事会围桌而坐，坐在首位、代表公司签字的那个人，把「坐前排」的字面安排原样保留在现代头衔里，因此同一个词也指董事长、总裁。

senses.title: The person who chairs a meeting
senses.definition: the person chosen to lead a meeting, a club, or an assembly
senses.definitionCN: 被推选出来主持聚会、俱乐部或集会的负责人
senses.example: The president of the club called for a vote.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部会长要求进行表决。
senses.why: This is the plainest surviving sense: the one who sits in front of the group, keeps order, and lets others speak in turn.
senses.whyCN: 这是最贴近字面的一个义项：坐在一群人前面、维持秩序、安排轮流发言的人；规模没有国家或公司那么大，却仍是「坐前排」的原样动作。

intro.en: President goes back to a Latin verb made of a prefix meaning in front and a verb meaning to sit; the title first named anyone who sat before a group, then the head of a state.
intro.cn: president 可追到由「在前」的前缀与「坐」的动词组成的拉丁语动词；这个头衔最初指坐在一群人前面的人，后来才指国家元首。

items.en: The prefix prae- meant before or in front, and it is the same element seen in many Latin words of rank and place.
items.cn: 前缀 prae- 意为「在前、在前面」，与许多表示位次和位置的拉丁词共用这一成分。

items.en: The verb sedere meant to sit, and it is the source of a wide family of English words about seats, sessions, and settling down.
items.cn: 动词 sedere 意为「坐」，派生出一大批关于座位、会议与安顿下来的英语词。

items.en: Praesidere joined the two: to sit before others, and therefore to watch over, guard, or lead an assembly.
items.cn: praesidere 把两者合起来：坐在别人前面，因此引申为看守、护卫、主持一个集会。

items.en: The present participle praesidens, with the stem praesident-, named the person who sits in front; this is the form English took.
items.cn: 现在分词 praesidens 的词干是 praesident-，指坐在前面的人，英语取用的正是这一形式。

items.en: Old French president passed the title into English, first for the officer of a meeting or a college, later for the head of a state and of a company.
items.cn: 古法语 president 把这个头衔传入英语，先指会议或学院的负责人，后来才指国家元首与公司最高负责人。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb for sitting in front; the near-meaning group gathers other titles for the person who leads a body.
note.cn: 形近组沿表示「坐在前面」的拉丁动词展开；近义组收其他称呼团体领导者的头衔。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin phrase turned into a title: the one who sits in front. Every sense keeps that seat at the head of the table.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是把一个拉丁短语变成头衔：「坐在前面的人」；每个义项都保留着长桌首位那把椅子。

normal.en: President is prae- plus sedere: the one who sits in front of the others.
normal.cn: president 是 prae- 加 sedere：坐在其他人前面的那个人。

normal.en: Preside is the verb underneath the title, and presidency names the office or the term.
normal.cn: preside 是头衔底下的动词，presidency 则指职位或任期。

normal.en: Presidential adds -ial to make the adjective, as in a presidential election.
normal.cn: presidential 加 -ial 构成形容词，例如 a presidential election（总统选举）。

normal.en: The same Latin verb gave presidium, a standing committee that also sits in front of a larger body.
normal.cn: 同一个拉丁动词也生出 presidium，指同样坐在更大机构前面的常设委员会。

normal.en: A club president and a company president share the title because both chair a body, not because both lead a country.
normal.cn: 俱乐部会长与公司董事长共用一个头衔，是因为两人都在主持一个团体，而不是因为两人都领导国家。

abstract.en: The oldest meaning is a seating plan: the person in the front chair gets to speak for everyone behind.
abstract.cn: 最古老的含义其实是一张座次表：坐在前面椅子上的人，替后面所有人说话。

abstract.en: Power in this word is drawn as a place at the table, which is why the same title fits a state, a school, and a firm.
abstract.cn: 这个词里的权力被画成「桌边的一个位置」，所以同一个头衔能装下国家、学校与公司。

abstract.en: Whenever a group needs one voice, it looks for someone to sit at the head of the table.
abstract.cn: 只要一个群体需要统一的声音，就会找一个人坐到长桌首位。

examples.cn: 总统通过电视向全国发表讲话。

examples.cn: 大学校长宣布典礼开始。

definition_en: a substance taken to treat or prevent illness, and also the science or practice of healing, including the branch that treats illness without surgery
core_image: 一只棕色玻璃药瓶放在一本翻开的厚医书上，瓶口的软木塞还留着药粉的痕迹
scene: 老式诊所的木架上，一只棕色药瓶和一本翻旧的医书并排放着，瓶身标签已经泛黄。 The old doctor said the medicine tasted bitter but worked quickly.
sceneCN: 这里是「药、药物」（第 1 个义项：服用的药）；句意为老医生说这药虽苦却见效快。图中可辨识物件：棕色药瓶、医书、木架。

derivatives.zh: 由 medicine 的词干 medic 加 -al 构成，义为「医学的；医疗的」
由同一词干加 -inal 构成，义为「药用的；有疗效的」
由 medicinal 加 -ly 构成，义为「作为药物地」
由同一词干加 -ment 构成，义为「药物；药剂」

senses.title: A substance taken to treat illness
senses.definition: a substance, especially one taken by mouth, used to treat or prevent illness
senses.definitionCN: 用来治疗或预防疾病的物质，尤指口服的
senses.example: Take this medicine after meals and keep it out of reach of children.
senses.exampleCN: 这药饭后服用，并放在孩子拿不到的地方。
senses.why: Latin medicina first named the healing art, and because the art needed materials, the word came to name the substances themselves.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 medicina 起初指医术，而医术需要材料，于是这个词也用来指那些材料本身。

senses.title: The science and practice of healing
senses.definition: the science and practice of diagnosing, treating and preventing disease
senses.definitionCN: 诊断、治疗与预防疾病的科学与实践
senses.example: She chose medicine because she wanted to understand how the body fails.
senses.exampleCN: 她选择学医，因为她想弄懂身体是怎样出故障的。
senses.why: The same Latin word named the art of healing as a whole, so the discipline kept the older, broader sense.
senses.whyCN: 同一个拉丁词本就指整体的医术，因此这一学科保留了更早、更宽的含义。

senses.title: The branch that avoids surgery
senses.definition: the branch of medicine that treats disease through drugs and diet rather than surgery
senses.definitionCN: 以药物与饮食而非手术来治病的医学分支，与外科相对
senses.example: He was moved from surgery to medicine when the operation was cancelled.
senses.exampleCN: 手术取消后，他从外科转到内科。
senses.why: When surgery split off as its own craft, the parent word stayed with the non-surgical side, so medicine also names that department.
senses.whyCN: 当外科独立成一门技艺，母词就留在不动刀的一边，于是 medicine 也指那个科室。

senses.title: Something that improves a bad situation
senses.definition: something that improves a difficult situation, used figuratively as if it were a cure
senses.definitionCN: 比喻能改善困境的事物，好像一剂解药
senses.example: Laughter is good medicine for a tired crew.
senses.exampleCN: 笑声对疲惫的船员是一剂良药。
senses.why: Anything that heals can be called medicine, so the word extends easily from pills to comfort, rest or humour.
senses.whyCN: 凡是能治病的东西都能叫 medicine，于是词义很自然地从药片延伸到安慰、休息或幽默。

intro.en: Medicine goes back to a Latin verb for healing, and the same root produced the doctor, the art and the substances, senses English still keeps apart.
intro.cn: medicine 可追溯到拉丁语表示医治的动词，同一词根生出医生、医术与药物，英语至今把这几个义项分开使用。

items.en: Mederi meant to heal, and it supplied the verb behind physician, remedy and medicine alike.
items.cn: mederi 意为医治，是 physician、remedy 与 medicine 共同的动词来源。

items.en: Medicus was the physician, and medicina was the healing art that this person practised.
items.cn: medicus 指医生，medicina 指这位医生所行的医术。

items.en: Medicina covered both the art of healing and the substances used in it, a double sense from the start.
items.cn: medicina 同时指医术与所用之物，从一开始就是双义。

items.en: Old French medecine kept both senses and handed them to English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 medecine 保留这两种含义，并在诺曼时期之后传给英语。

items.en: English medicine now leans on drugs in daily speech, while the discipline and the hospital department keep the older sense.
items.cn: 现代英语里 medicine 在日常口语中偏向药物，而学科与医院科室保留较早的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words from the same healing root; the near-meaning group collects drugs, remedies and forms of care.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「医治」词根的词；近义组收药物、疗法与照护方式。

entries.definition: Having healing properties, used of herbs or substances rather than the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 有疗效的，多用于草药或物质，而非学科。

entries.definition: Relating to the science or practice of healing.
entries.definitionCN: 与医治的科学或实践有关。

entries.definition: A formal term for a substance used to heal.
entries.definitionCN: 指治病物质的正式说法。

entries.definition: Drugs prescribed for a condition, or the course of taking them.
entries.definitionCN: 为某种病情开出的药，或服药的疗程。

entries.definition: A substance used to treat illness or, differently, one taken for pleasure.
entries.definitionCN: 用于治病的物质；也可指为快感而用的毒品。

entries.definition: A treatment that cures or relieves a complaint.
entries.definitionCN: 能治愈或缓解病痛的疗法。

entries.definition: A treatment that ends a disease, or the state of being healed.
entries.definitionCN: 终结疾病的疗法；也指痊愈的状态。

entries.definition: A small dose of medicine shaped for swallowing.
entries.definitionCN: 便于吞服的小剂型药物。

entries.definition: The care and procedures used against an illness.
entries.definitionCN: 针对疾病采取的照护与处置。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb for healing; its family keeps returning to the doctor, the art, the substance and the department.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示医治的拉丁动词上，同族词反复回到医生、医术、药物与科室。

normal.en: Mederi in Latin means to heal, and medicine is the whole effort built on that verb.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mederi 意为医治，medicine 就是建立在这个动词上的整套努力。

normal.en: Medicus is the doctor; medicina is both the art and what the art uses.
normal.cn: medicus 是医生，medicina 既是医术，也是医术所用的东西。

normal.en: Medical adds -al and describes the field, not a bottle of pills.
normal.cn: medical 加 -al，描述的是这个领域，而不是一瓶药。

normal.en: Medicinal adds -inal and means having the power to heal.
normal.cn: medicinal 加 -inal，意为具有治病效力。

normal.en: The department sense survives in hospital signs, where medicine stands opposite surgery.
normal.cn: 科室义保存在医院标牌上，medicine 与 surgery 相对。

abstract.en: One word holds the art, the pill and the ward, because healing needs knowledge, material and a place to happen.
abstract.cn: 一个词装下了医术、药片与病房，因为治病需要知识、材料与发生的场所。

abstract.en: Calling laughter medicine shows that the word measures not the substance but the relief it brings.
abstract.cn: 把笑声称作良药，说明这个词衡量的不是物质，而是它带来的缓解。

abstract.en: A word that can mean both a science and a bottle reminds us that cure is always part knowledge and part matter.
abstract.cn: 一个词既能指科学又能指药瓶，提醒人治愈总是半靠知识、半靠物质。

examples.en: The medicine worked within an hour and the fever broke.
examples.cn: 药一小时内起效，烧退了。

examples.en: He wants to study medicine in a city hospital.
examples.cn: 他想在城市医院学医。

examples.en: Keep the medicine in a cool, dry place.
examples.cn: 把药放在阴凉干燥处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没事的」——吃了药就没事的；记住 medicine 是药。

root: 拉丁语 mederi（医治）→ medicus（医生）→ medicina（医术、药物），经古法语 medecine 进入英语；同族词多与治疗有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is healing; the senses divide into the substance, the discipline, the hospital branch and the figurative comfort.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是医治；义项分为药物、学科、医院科室与比喻性的安慰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brown glass bottle standing on an open medical book, cork still dusted with powder.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只棕色玻璃药瓶放在一本翻开的厚医书上，瓶口的软木塞还留着药粉的痕迹。

branches.en: a spoon of syrup held out to a child
branches.cn: 递到孩子面前的一勺糖浆

branches.en: a laugh that loosens a tense room
branches.cn: 让紧绷的房间松下来的笑声

branches.en: a lecture hall full of diagrams of the body
a hospital corridor sign pointing away from surgery
branches.cn: 医院走廊里指离外科的指示牌

branches.en: a ward round where pills are checked against charts
branches.cn: 按记录核对药片的查房

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin verb of healing, the doctor noun, the noun for the art, the French form and English endings that build adjectives.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示医治的拉丁动词、指医生的名词、指医术的名词、法语形式，以及构成形容词的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_en: an action that is against the law and can be punished
core_image: 越过法律红线的行为
scene: 法制课上，警察叔叔讲了一个偷盗电瓶车的小案子。 Stealing a bike is a crime and can lead to prison.
sceneCN: 这里 crime 是「犯罪；罪行」（第 1 个义项：违法且会受罚的行为）；句意是偷自行车是犯罪，可能坐牢。

derivatives.zh: 由 crime 加后缀构成，义为「罪犯」；也作形容词「犯罪的」
criminal 的复数，义为「多名罪犯」
由 crime 加 -ology 构成，义为「犯罪学」

senses.title: An act against the law
senses.definition: something you can be punished for by law, such as stealing or hurting someone
senses.definitionCN: 法律可以惩罚的行为，如偷窃或伤人
senses.example: The police wrote down every detail at the crime scene.
senses.exampleCN: 警察在犯罪现场记录下每个细节。
senses.why: The core image is crossing a line drawn by law, so any punished illegal act is a crime.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是越过法律画的线，所以任何会被惩罚的违法行为都是 crime。

senses.title: A very wrong or regrettable act
senses.definition: something very bad or wrong, even if not illegal
senses.definitionCN: 非常错误或可惜的事，即使不违法
senses.example: Wasting so much good food is a crime.
senses.exampleCN: 浪费这么多好食物简直是罪过。
senses.why: The line of law is borrowed as a line of morality, so a deep wrong is called a crime even without police.
senses.whyCN: 法律的线被借作道德的线，所以即使没有警察，大错也被称为 crime。

intro.en: Crime comes from a Latin word for a charge or judgement.
intro.cn: crime 来自一个表示指控或裁断的拉丁词。

items.en: The Latin crimen meant a charge, accusation or the point of a judgement.
items.cn: 拉丁语 crimen 意为指控、罪名或裁断要点。

items.en: It is thought to be related to cernere, to sift or decide.
items.cn: 一般认为它与 cernere（筛分、裁断）相关。

items.en: Old French turned it into crime, meaning a fault or offence.
items.cn: 古法语将其变为 crime，指过错、冒犯。

items.en: English borrowed crime in the thirteenth century for punishable offences.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 crime，指可惩罚的罪行。

items.en: Today crime covers police cases and moral blame alike.
items.cn: 如今 crime 既指警方案件，也指道德指责。

note.en: These words share the crime family or name wrong acts.
note.cn: 这些词属于 crime 词族，或指错误行为。

entries.definition: a person who commits crimes; also the adjective
entries.definitionCN: 罪犯；犯罪的

entries.definition: the study of crime
entries.definitionCN: 犯罪学

entries.definition: a dairy word; spelled almost alike, different root
entries.definitionCN: 奶油（拼写几乎相同，词源不同）

entries.definition: a deep red colour; sounds similar, different root
entries.definitionCN: 深红色（读音相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: an illegal act, often smaller
entries.definitionCN: 冒犯；违法行为

entries.definition: a wrong against moral law
entries.definitionCN: 罪过

entries.definition: stealing
entries.definitionCN: 偷窃

entries.definition: unlawful killing
entries.definitionCN: 谋杀

entries.definition: bad or illegal behaviour
entries.definitionCN: 恶行；不法行为

normalIntro.en: The judgement root and the crime family keep the word clear.
normalIntro.cn: 「裁断」词根和 crime 词族让词义清晰。

normal.en: crimen = a charge laid before a judge.
normal.cn: crimen ＝递到法官面前的指控。

normal.en: commit a crime: the fixed verb phrase.
normal.cn: commit a crime：固定动词搭配。

normal.en: criminal adds a suffix for the person and the adjective.
normal.cn: criminal 加后缀，既指人也作形容词。

normal.en: crime scene is where the line was crossed.
normal.cn: crime scene 是越过红线的地方。

normal.en: Do not confuse crime with cream, only one letter apart.
normal.cn: 别把 crime 和 cream 混淆，只差一个字母。

abstract.en: See a bright red line on the road of rules; stepping over it is the picture.
abstract.cn: 看规则之路上一条醒目的红线，踩过它就是画面本身。

abstract.en: Hear the gavel fall after the charge is read.
abstract.cn: 听指控宣读后法槌落下。

abstract.en: Picture a spoiled feast thrown away while others go hungry.
abstract.cn: 想象别人挨饿时被糟蹋的盛宴，那是浪费之「罪」。

examples.en: Reporting a crime quickly helps the police.
examples.cn: 快速报案能帮助警方。

examples.en: The crime rate in our town fell this year.
examples.cn: 今年我们镇的犯罪率下降了。

examples.en: Lying to ruin a classmate's name is a kind of crime against trust.
examples.cn: 用谎言毁掉同学名声是对信任的一种「罪」。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克莱姆」——跨过法律红线，判罚「克」不容情

root: 来自拉丁语 crimen（指控、罪名，一般认为与 cernere「裁断」相关），经古法语 crime 进入英语；核心意象是「被法庭记下的越界行为」。

sensesIntro.en: From punished illegal acts to moral wrongs that need no court.
sensesIntro.cn: 从受惩罚的违法行为，到无需法庭的道德罪过。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of law that must not be crossed
core.cn: 核心意象：不可跨越的法律红线

intro.cn: crime 领导着一个关于罪责与裁断的小词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root cernere means to sift and decide.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 cernere 意为筛分、裁断。

definition_en: a solid food made from milk, pressed into blocks and left to ripen
core_image: 一块压得紧紧的黄色奶块，越放越香
scene: 超市冷柜前，妈妈挑了一块硬质奶酪准备做三明治。 The hard cheese was cut into thin slices for the sandwiches.
sceneCN: 这里 cheese 是「奶酪」（第 1 个义项：用奶做的固体食品）；句意为硬奶酪被切成薄片夹进三明治。

derivatives.zh: 由 cheese 加 cake 构成，义为「芝士蛋糕」
由 cheese 加后缀构成，义为「满是奶酪的」

senses.title: A solid food made from milk
senses.definition: a food made by pressing and ripening the thick part of milk
senses.definitionCN: 把牛奶中的稠厚部分压制成形并熟成而得的食品
senses.example: The hard cheese was cut into thin slices for the sandwiches.
senses.exampleCN: 硬奶酪被切成薄片夹进三明治。
senses.why: The word names the pressed milk product directly, by what it is made of and how it is made.
senses.whyCN: 这个词直接按原料与制法命名：压制成形的奶制品。

senses.title: A specific kind or shape of cheese
senses.definition: one particular type of cheese, such as cream cheese
senses.definitionCN: 某种特定的奶酪，如奶油奶酪
senses.example: Many soft cheeses come from France.
senses.exampleCN: 许多软质奶酪产自法国。
senses.why: A general product easily divides into kinds, each keeping the product's name with a new head noun.
senses.whyCN: 泛指的产品容易分化为品种，各品种沿用产品之名再配新修饰语。

senses.title: A smile posed for a photo
senses.definition: the forced smile people make when a photographer says 'say cheese'
senses.definitionCN: 摄影师喊「说 cheese」时人们摆出的笑容
senses.example: Everyone said cheese and the photo froze their grins.
senses.exampleCN: 大家齐喊「茄子」，照片定格了他们的笑容。
senses.why: Because the word pulls the mouth wide like a smile, it became the standard photo cue.
senses.whyCN: 念这个词时口型拉开像笑，于是成了拍照的固定口令。

intro.en: Cheese goes back to a Latin word for pressed milk, carried through Old English.
intro.cn: cheese 可追溯到拉丁语中指压制奶制品的词，经古英语传承下来。

items.en: Latin caseus meant cheese, the milk pressed into solid form.
items.cn: 拉丁语 caseus 指奶酪，即压制成固体的奶。

items.en: Early Germanic borrowed it as *kasjus, spreading through trade.
items.cn: 早期日耳曼语借为 *kasjus，随商贸传播。

items.en: Old English cyse or cies meant the milk food.
items.cn: 古英语 cyse、cies 指这种奶制食品。

items.en: Middle English settled the spelling as cheese.
items.cn: 中古英语将拼写定型为 cheese。

items.en: Modern English cheese names hundreds of kinds and even the photo smile.
items.cn: 现代英语的 cheese 涵盖数百种奶酪，甚至衍生出拍照的微笑义。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects dairy foods.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收乳制品类词。

entries.definition: A shout of joy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词/动词，义为「欢呼」，读音与 cheese 相近。

entries.definition: The side of the face.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「脸颊」，拼写与 cheese 相近。

entries.definition: Like cheese; old-fashioned and overly sentimental.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「像奶酪的；俗套的」，由 cheese 派生。

entries.definition: A soft yellow fat made from milk.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「黄油」，同属奶制品。

entries.definition: A thick, slightly sour milk food.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「酸奶」，同属奶制品。

entries.definition: The white drink from cows.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「牛奶」，是奶酪的原料。

normalIntro.cn: 借助词根与词族记忆 cheese。

definition_en: something that people do, or the state of being busy
core_image: 学生们在操场上做各种活动
scene: 下午的校园里，学生们参加各种课外活动。 The school offers many activities after class.
sceneCN: 这里 activities 是「课外活动」（第 1 个义项：人们做的事）；句意为学校课后提供许多活动。

积极地
使活动；激活

senses.title: Something people do
senses.definition: a thing that people spend time doing
senses.definitionCN: 人们花时间去做的事情
senses.example: Sport is my favourite activity.
senses.exampleCN: 运动是我最喜欢的活动。
senses.why: Activity is the noun of active, so it names a thing that keeps people active.
senses.whyCN: activity 是 active 的名词，指让人保持活动的一件事。

senses.title: A state of busy movement
senses.definition: the state of being busy and full of movement
senses.definitionCN: 忙碌而充满动静的状态
senses.example: The market was full of activity.
senses.exampleCN: 市场里一片繁忙。
senses.why: The adjective active became a noun of state, which gives the sense of busy movement.
senses.whyCN: 把 active 的状态抽象成名词，就得到繁忙活跃的意思。

intro.en: The recorded history of activity is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 activity 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Agere meant to do, and it stands behind the whole family of words.
items.cn: agere 意为做，是整个词族的来源。

items.en: Activus meant busy or working.
items.cn: activus 意为忙碌的、运作的。

items.en: English formed active first, then added a noun ending.
items.cn: 英语先构成 active，再加名词词尾。

items.en: Activity named the state of being busy and the things done.
items.cn: activity 指忙碌的状态以及所做的事。

items.en: Today schools use the plural for clubs and sports.
items.cn: 今天学校用复数形式指社团与体育活动。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: More than one thing that people do.
entries.definitionCN: 指多项人们做的事。

entries.definition: The adjective for being busy or moving.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指忙碌或活动的。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to set something working.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，意为使某物开始运作。

entries.definition: It stresses doing rather than being busy.
entries.definitionCN: 强调行动本身，而非忙碌状态。

entries.definition: It stresses an activity someone gives time to.
entries.definitionCN: 强调投入时间的活动。

entries.definition: It stresses the working of a system.
entries.definitionCN: 强调系统的运作。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: active means doing things, and -ity names the doing: activity is what keeps someone busy.
normal.cn: active 表示做事，-ity 表示这种状态：activity 就是让人忙碌的事。

normal.en: The same family also gives active and actively.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 active 与 actively。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase after-school activity.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「课外活动」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of activity in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 activity 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: something that people do, or the state of being busy.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「活动」时用它。

abstract.en: Picture students doing many things on a school ground.
abstract.cn: 想象学生们在操场上做各种活动。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

examples.en: Sport is my favourite activity.
examples.cn: 运动是我最喜欢的活动。

examples.en: The market was full of activity.
examples.cn: 市场里一片繁忙。

examples.en: The club plans an outdoor activity for Sunday.
examples.cn: 俱乐部为周日安排了一项户外活动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克提维提」——学生在操场上做各种活动：活动

root: activity 由 active 加名词词尾 -ity 构成。active 来自拉丁语 activus「忙碌的、运作的」，由动词 agere「做」而来；activity 指忙碌的状态以及所做的事，今天学校常用复数形式指社团与体育活动。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of activity grows from one core image: students doing many things on a school ground.
sensesIntro.cn: activity 的各个义项都从同一个核心意象生长出来：学生们在操场上做各种活动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: students doing many things on a school ground
core.cn: 核心意象：学生们在操场上做各种活动

branches.en: Sense 01 covers the most literal use: Something people do.
branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖最字面的用法：一项活动。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers a wider everyday use: A state of busy movement.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：繁忙活跃的状态。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 02 covers the two main uses: Something people do / A state of busy movement.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖两个主要用法：一项活动、繁忙活跃的状态。

branches.en: Sense 01 covers a later use: Something people do.
branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖再往后的一种用法：一项活动。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers the outer edge of the meaning: A state of busy movement.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖意义的边缘：繁忙活跃的状态。

intro.en: activity can be split into the parts below, which also connect it to common English patterns.
intro.cn: activity 可以按下面的成分拆开，这些成分也把它与常见的英语构词方式连起来。

latinIntro.en: No recorded Latin cognate is securely attached to this word, so the list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠记录的拉丁同族词可以系在这个词上，因此该列表留空。

items.example: It comes from agere, meaning to do.

items.exampleCN: 它构成表倾向的形容词。

items.example: It forms abstract nouns of state.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表状态的抽象名词。

items.example: It marks a plural noun in English.
It marks the past tense or a completed state.
items.exampleCN: 它标记过去时或已完成的状态。

items.example: It forms the present participle of a verb.
items.exampleCN: 它构成动词的现在分词。

items.example: It turns an adjective into an adverb.
It names the doer of an action.
items.exampleCN: 它指做某动作的人或物。

derivatives.zh: 活跃的；积极的
积极地
使活动；激活

definition_zh: 重要的；重大的；有影响力的
definition_en: having a great effect or value, and therefore deserving attention, care, or respect
core_image: 一张被反复推到桌子正中央的纸条，上面写着「这件事必须做」
scene: 开工前的班前会上，班长把一张写着安全要求的纸推到桌子正中，拍了拍。 Safety, he stressed, is the important part.
sceneCN: 这里 important 是「重要的、重大的」（第 1 个义项：分量重、必须重视），句意是班长强调，安全才是最要紧的那一部分。画面里有班前会、一张被推到桌子中央的纸条和班长的手。

pos.zh: 形容词：重要的、重大的；有影响力的

derivatives.zh: 重要性、重要意义
重要地；重要的是
不重要的、无关紧要的

senses.title: Mattering a great deal
senses.definition: having a great effect or value, so that it deserves care and attention
senses.definitionCN: 影响或价值很大，因而值得用心对待
senses.example: Sleep is important for children who are still growing.
senses.exampleCN: 对还在长身高的孩子来说，睡眠很重要。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense: the thing carries weight and should not be ignored.
senses.whyCN: 这是最日常的义项：事情有分量，不能被忽略。

senses.title: Powerful or influential
senses.definition: having power or a high position in an organization or a field
senses.definitionCN: 在某个组织或领域里有权势、地位高
senses.example: She is an important figure in the city's music scene.
senses.exampleCN: 她在这个城市的音乐圈里是个有分量的人物。
senses.why: The weight spreads from the matter to the person who controls it, so the adjective describes people too.
senses.whyCN: 分量从事延伸到掌握事的人身上，于是这个形容词也能形容人。

senses.title: Solemn or self-asserting
senses.definition: used of a tone or manner that treats small things as very serious
senses.definitionCN: 形容一种把小事故意当成大事的语气或神态
senses.example: He gave an important nod before opening the envelope.
senses.exampleCN: 他煞有介事地点了点头，才拆开信封。
senses.why: Once a word for weight, it can also describe someone who plays at carrying weight.
senses.whyCN: 原本说分量的词，也能形容装出分量的人。

intro.en: Important is the adjective of import, which comes from the Latin verb for carrying something in.
intro.cn: important 是 import 的形容词形式，而 import 源自拉丁语中表示「搬进来」的动词。

items.en: Importare joined in, into, with portare, to carry, and meant to bring something in.
items.cn: 拉丁语 importare 把 in「进入」与 portare「搬运」组合起来，意为「把东西搬进来」。

items.en: Scholars used the verb for matters that carry meaning, so importare grew to mean to signify.
items.cn: 学者们用它来说「承载意义」的事，于是 importare 渐渐有了「意味着、关系重大」的意思。

items.en: French built the adjective important from the same stem, describing something of consequence.
items.cn: 法语由同一词干造出形容词 important，形容有后果、有关系的事物。

items.en: English adopted important in the sixteenth century, first in formal writing about serious matters.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收 important，最初多见于谈论严肃事务的正式文章。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the adjective had spread into everyday speech and now covers people as well as things.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，这个形容词已进入日常口语，如今既能修饰事，也能修饰人。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the import family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives with overlapping force.
note.cn: 形近组收 import 一族词；近义组收语义相近、强度不同的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of mattering.
entries.definitionCN: 名词形式，指「重要性」。

entries.definition: The adverb, used at the start of a sentence to add weight to a point.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式，常置于句首为某一点加重分量。

entries.definition: The verb and noun about bringing in goods from other countries.
entries.definitionCN: 指「进口」的动词与名词，与 important 同源但侧重货物。

entries.definition: Large enough to be noticed and to affect a result.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「显著的、有意义的」，强调大到能被察觉并影响结果。

entries.definition: So important that something cannot work without it.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「必不可少的」，强调缺了就根本不行。

entries.definition: Deciding the outcome at one particular point.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「关键的」，指在某个节点上决定结果。

normalIntro.en: The hooks work on the carried-in root and on the phrases that English has fixed around the adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子围绕「搬进来」的词根，以及英语中已经固定下来的搭配来展开。

normal.en: important shares its root with import, and both are about what gets carried into the centre.
normal.cn: important 与 import 同根，说的都是被搬到正中央的东西。

normal.en: Make it a habit to say it is important to, followed by a verb in the base form.
normal.cn: 记住句型 it is important to 后面接动词原形。

normal.en: More important and most important take extra words rather than -er and -est.
normal.cn: 比较级和最高级用 more、most，而不是加 -er、-est。

normal.en: An important role is a part in a task that the task cannot do without.
normal.cn: an important role 就是任务里少了它就做不成的那一份。

normal.en: Someone who is important in a field is not just busy but has weight in decisions.
normal.cn: 在某个领域里重要的人，不只是忙，而是在决定中有分量。

abstract.en: Importance is assigned by plans: what a plan depends on becomes important.
abstract.cn: 重要性由计划分配：计划所依赖的东西就变得重要。

abstract.en: The same word covers the serious and the pompous, so tone does much of the work.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既说郑重，也说装样子，因此大半靠语气来区分。

abstract.en: Calling something important is a small act of power, since it decides what people look at.
abstract.cn: 说某件事重要，本身就是一种小小的权力，因为它决定了大家看什么。

examples.en: It is important to check the figures twice before publishing the report.
examples.cn: 公布报告前，把数据核对两遍很重要。

examples.en: Her grandmother played an important role in her education.
examples.cn: 她的祖母在她的教育中起了重要作用。

examples.en: He tried hard to look important while holding the small envelope.
examples.cn: 他拿着那个小信封，努力装出一副总揽大局的样子。

dict_mnemonic.text: import 搬进来 + -ant 形容词词尾——值得搬上台面的，就是重要的

root: 拉丁语 importare「搬进来」（in + portare「搬运」）经中世纪拉丁语「关系重大」的引申、法语 important 进入英语，十六世纪起用于正式书面语，后进入日常口语并扩展到形容人物地位。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: mattering a great deal, having power in a field, and a manner that treats small things as great.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：事情分量重，某人在领域内有分量，以及把小事故意做大的神态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slip of paper pushed to the centre of the table because everything today hangs on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张纸条被推到桌子正中央，因为今天的一切都系于它。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT: important describes things that must not be ignored.
branches.cn: 分量线：important 形容不可忽略的事物。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the adjective moves from matters to people with power.
branches.cn: 人物线：这个形容词从事转到有权势的人身上。

branches.en: THE ACT: an important nod is weight performed rather than carried.
branches.cn: 表演线：important 的一点头，是演出来的分量而非真分量。

branches.en: THE PATTERN: it is important to plus a verb is the most fixed frame.
branches.cn: 句型线：it is important to 加动词原形是最固定的框架。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: importance and importantly carry the same root into other word classes.
branches.cn: 词族线：importance 与 importantly 把同一词根带进别的词类。

intro.en: The table puts the -ant adjective ending next to the -ance and -ly forms of the family.
intro.cn: 此表把 -ant 形容词词尾放在同族的 -ance、-ly 形式旁边对照。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is importare, built from in and portare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语底子是 importare，由 in 与 portare 组成。

items.example: This letter is important, so keep it safe.
They spoke about the importance of honesty.
items.exampleCN: 他们谈到了诚实的重要。
重要的是，全队达成了一致。

items.example: That is an unimportant detail for now.
items.exampleCN: 眼下那是个不重要的细节。

items.meaning: to send goods out of a country
items.example: The firm exports machines to Africa.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司向非洲出口机器。

items.example: The beam supports the whole roof.
items.exampleCN: 这根梁支撑着整个屋顶。

items.example: A portable lamp lit the tent.
items.exampleCN: 一盏便携灯照亮了帐篷。

latinEntries.meaning: a harbour, a place where goods are carried in
latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语名词：港口，货物搬进之处

definition_en: to talk in a friendly, informal way; a friendly informal conversation
core_image: 两个朋友凑在一起，轻松随意地说着话
scene: 课间休息时，同桌凑过来聊起周末的篮球赛。 We had a short chat about the basketball game during the break.
sceneCN: 这里 chat 是「闲聊」（第 1 个义项：轻松随意的谈话）；句意为课间我们聊了一会儿篮球赛。

derivatives.zh: 由 chat 加 -y 构成，义为「爱闲聊的；闲谈式的」
由 chat 加 room 构成，义为「聊天室」

senses.title: To talk in a friendly informal way
senses.definition: to talk with someone in a friendly, relaxed way about small things
senses.definitionCN: 以友好轻松的方式与人谈论日常小事
senses.example: We chatted about the basketball game after class.
senses.exampleCN: 课后我们聊起了篮球赛。
senses.why: The word pictures the light, repeated noise of small birds, matching easy small talk between friends.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原画的是小鸟轻快的鸣叫，正像朋友间轻松的闲话。

senses.title: A friendly informal conversation
senses.definition: a short, friendly and informal talk
senses.definitionCN: 一次短暂、友好且随意的谈话
senses.example: She gave me a quick chat before the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前她和我快速聊了几句。
senses.why: The action of chatting easily names the talk itself, a normal move from act to event.
senses.whyCN: 闲聊的动作顺理成章命名了谈话本身，是常见的由行为转事件。

senses.title: Talking online by typing messages
senses.definition: exchanging typed messages with others on the internet in real time
senses.definitionCN: 通过互联网实时互发文字消息交流
senses.example: They chat in the class group every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 他们每晚都在班级群里聊天。
senses.why: Typing on a screen feels like talking, so the old word of light talk moved onto the screen.
senses.whyCN: 在屏幕上打字如同说话，古老的轻谈一词便迁移到了屏幕上。

intro.en: Chat is a shortened, chirping form of chatter, first used for birds and then for people.
intro.cn: chat 是 chatter 的简短形式，最早形容鸟叫，后来用于人。

items.en: Old English ceatt was an echoic word, imitating small noises.
items.cn: 古英语 ceatt 是拟声词，模仿细碎的声音。

items.en: Middle English chater meant to make quick, repeated sounds, like birds or teeth.
items.cn: 中古英语 chater 指发出快速重复的声音，如鸟鸣或牙齿打颤。

items.en: Chatter applied to people talking rapidly about nothing important.
items.cn: chatter 开始形容人絮絮叨叨地谈琐事。

items.en: The short form chat appeared, meaning easy friendly talk.
items.cn: 简短形式 chat 出现，意为轻松友好的交谈。

items.en: Modern English chat covers spoken small talk and typed online talk.
items.cn: 现代英语的 chat 涵盖口头闲谈与在线文字聊天。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects talking words.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收谈话类词。

entries.definition: To act dishonestly to win.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「欺骗；作弊」，拼写与 chat 仅差一字母。

entries.definition: To talk quickly about unimportant things.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「喋喋不休」，由同根派生。

entries.definition: Something you wear on your head.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「帽子」，读音与 chat 词尾相近。

entries.definition: To speak with someone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「谈话」，泛指说话交流。

entries.definition: To talk about other people's private lives.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「闲话；说长道短」，与 chat 相近但略带贬义。

entries.definition: To talk with someone, more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「交谈」，较 chat 正式。

normalIntro.en: Remember chat by its root and family.
normalIntro.cn: 借助词根与词族记忆 chat。

normal.en: chat is the short form of chatter.
normal.cn: chat 是 chatter 的简短形式。

normal.en: chatroom is where people chat online.
normal.cn: chatroom 是网上聊天的地方。

normal.en: chatty describes a talkative person.
normal.cn: chatty 形容爱聊天的人。

normal.en: have a chat is a natural everyday phrase.
normal.cn: have a chat 是地道的日常说法。

normal.en: birds chat too: the word first copied their sound.
normal.cn: 鸟也「聊天」：这个词最初就是模仿鸟叫。

abstract.en: Picture two birds trading quick little notes on a branch.
abstract.cn: 想象两只小鸟在枝头你来我往地短促鸣叫。

abstract.en: Hear soft laughter mixed into the lunchtime noise.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见午餐时间的喧闹里混着轻笑声。

abstract.en: Feel the message bubbles popping up one after another.
abstract.cn: 感受聊天气泡一条接一条弹出。

examples.en: We had a short chat about the basketball game during the break.
examples.cn: 课间我们简短地聊了一会儿篮球赛。

examples.en: She loves to chat with her friends on the way home.
examples.cn: 她喜欢在放学路上和朋友们聊天。

examples.en: They chatted in the class group until bedtime.
examples.cn: 他们在班级群里聊到睡觉时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「岔特」——话题岔来岔去特别多，这就是闲聊。

root: 拟声来源：古英语 ceatt（拟声）→ 中古英语 chater（喋喋不休）→ 短化形式 chat → 现代英语 chat；同族词有 chatter（喋喋不休）、chatty（爱闲谈的）。

sensesIntro.en: Chat moves from bird-like quick sounds to easy talk, the talk itself, and typed online talk.
sensesIntro.cn: chat 由鸟般的轻快叫声转为轻松谈话、谈话本身，再到在线文字交流。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: quick light noise, like birds, between friends
core.cn: 核心意象：朋友间如鸟鸣般轻快的细碎声音

intro.cn: chat 是拟声词，源于声音而非拉丁词根。

latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁同族词，词族是拟声的 chatter 一系。

items.meaning: to talk quickly about small things
items.example: The girls chattered about the film.
items.exampleCN: 女孩们叽叽喳喳聊电影。

items.example: The old chatrooms are quiet now.
items.exampleCN: 昔日的聊天室如今冷清了。

items.meaning: a program that talks with people

items.example: Let us have a chat after lunch.
We exchanged chit-chat at the door.
items.exampleCN: 我们在门口寒暄了几句。

items.example: Our class chat group is busy.
items.exampleCN: 我们班的聊天群很热闹。

definition_en: to find the answer to a problem, puzzle, or difficulty
core_image: 一个人把缠成一团的绳子一点点解开
scene: 他们花了一小时才解决那道谜题。 They spent an hour trying to solve the puzzle.
sceneCN: 这里 solve 是「解答；破解」（第 2 个义项）；句意：他们花了一小时才解决那道谜题。

derivatives.zh: 解决办法；解答
可解决的
解题者；解决者
未解决的

senses.title: Fix a problem
senses.definition: to find a way to deal with a problem or difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 找到处理问题或困难的办法
senses.example: The team solved the problem in one meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 团队开了一次会就解决了问题。
senses.why: The Latin root means to loosen, and a problem is a knot.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「松开」，而问题正像一个绳结。

senses.title: Find the answer
senses.definition: to find the correct answer to a puzzle or question
senses.definitionCN: 找出谜题或问题的正确答案
senses.example: They spent an hour trying to solve the puzzle.
senses.exampleCN: 他们花了一小时才解决那道谜题。
senses.why: A puzzle is another kind of knot for the mind.
senses.whyCN: 谜题是另一种打给头脑的结。

senses.title: Crack a case
senses.definition: to discover the truth about something difficult, such as a crime
senses.definitionCN: 查明困难事情的真相，例如案件
senses.example: The detective solved the crime in two days.
senses.exampleCN: 侦探两天就破了案。
senses.why: Loosening a mystery means uncovering what was hidden.
senses.whyCN: 解开谜团，就是揭示被隐藏的东西。

intro.en: Solve comes from a Latin verb meaning to loosen or untie.
intro.cn: solve 来自拉丁语中表示松开、解开的动词。

items.en: Solvere meant to loosen, untie, or dissolve.
items.cn: solvere 意为松开、解开或溶解。

items.en: Solutio named a loosening or an explanation.
items.cn: solutio 指解开或解释。

items.en: English used solve for explaining difficult matters.
items.cn: 英语用 solve 表示解释困难的事情。

items.en: It specialized in answering problems and puzzles.
items.cn: 它专门用于回答问题和谜题。

items.en: It extended to cracking crimes and mysteries.
items.cn: 它的用途扩展到破解案件和谜团。

branches.cn: 谜题与难题都在同一种耐心面前让步。
